item.description: The father of one of the 19 young abductees tells the BBC he hasn't eaten in three days out of worry.

item.title: Africanews: Pix of the Day, 5 October, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Pix of the Day, 5 October, 2026 - Across the world

item.title: BBC Africa: Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
item.description: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.

item.title: Africanews: Nobel Prize in medicine awarded to three scientists for breakthrough research
item.description: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.

item.title: Africanews: A new UN Chief, an old institution and a world in crisis
item.description: The next UN secretary-general will take charge of an institution under pressure to restore its influence, tackle financial challenges and adapt to a changing world.

item.title: Africanews: Food prices rising in Kenya as climate change strains supply
item.description: Climate change has started hitting the food markets in Kenya and shoppers are feeling the pinch. In the capital Nairobi and across much of the country, rising prices are forcing consumers to make tough choices - buying and eating less.

item.title: Africanews: Guinea opposition leader Aliou Bah freed after presidential pardon
item.description: Guinean opposition politician Aliou Bah, who was jailed for insulting junta leader General Mamadi Doumbouya, was granted a presidential pardon Friday after nearly two years behind bars.

item.title: Africanews: Brazil's presidential election heads to runoff between Bolsonara and Lula
item.description: Brazil presidential candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro and incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will face off in a runoff October 25 for the top job after neither won a majority in Sunday's vote.

item.title: Africanews: Spain begins dismantling migrant camp on Ceuta beach
item.description: Authorities began on Sunday to remove a migrant camp on the beach of Ceuta, Spain's enclave in North Africa, ahead of a mid-October visit by Spain's king and queen, police said.

item.title: Africanews: Yemeni government forces launch major offensive to retake Houthi-held territory
item.description: Government forces in Yemen have launched a major military operation to retake the territory seized by Houthi rebels last month.

item.title: Africanews: Ethiopia's federal forces retake Tigrayan capital Mekelle
item.description: Ethiopian federal forces were in full control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, a local journalist said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

item.title: Africanews: Iran sets up military training camp for volunteers in face of US threats
item.description: Iran on Saturday inaugurated a second makeshift military training base in the capital Tehran, in a show of defiance as the US threatens to "blow up" and "annihilate" Iran.

item.title: BBC Africa: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election
item.description: A voter mobilisation campaign has registered huge numbers of young people but it is not clear who they are backing.

item.title: Africanews: Eight countries including China join military exercises in Russia
item.description: Troops from eight countries including China have been participating in joint military exercises in Russia. The exercise concluded on Saturday after conducting coordinated ground and air operations, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

item.title: BBC Africa: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
item.description: Two residents in Mekelle tell the BBC pro-government forces have taken control of the city.

item.title: Africanews: Persistent violence stalling African development, Burundi's Ndayishimiye tells summit
item.description: Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye says at an African Union meeting in El Alamein, Egypt, that persistent violence across Africa is taking a toll on farming, education and development.

item.title: Africanews: Ethiopian forces recapture Mekelle airport from Tigrayan fighters
item.description: Ethiopian federal forces have taken Mekelle airport, reversing a takeover by Tigrayan fighters last month.

item.title: Africanews: Houthi rebels claim attack on Saudi oil facility in Riyadh
item.description: Yemen’s Houthi rebels on Saturday claimed attacks against facilities of Aramco, the world's largest oil company, in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh.

item.title: Africanews: Ethiopia’s Oromo celebrate Irreecha and call for peace as federal forces enter Mekelle
item.description: Tens of thousands of Oromo gathered in Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa on Saturday to celebrate the thanksgiving festival of Irreecha. The gathering took place amid reports that federal forces had entered Mekelle, the capital of the northern region of Tigray.

item.title: Africanews: African leaders call for continent to unlock capital at Egypt business summit
item.description: African heads of state and business leaders gathered in Egypt on Saturday for the inaugural El-Alamein Africa Forum. They called for the continent to unlock its capital to finance growth and reduce reliance on external funding.
